clue.text: It has a brush with destiny of mortal and immortal

parts.note: 'dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return': dust is the fate of mortal humans
Pan is an immortal Greek god

explanation.surface: Someone shares in the fate of both mortals and gods, a brush with destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a brush with destiny' reads as a near miss with fate, but the definition is the thing a brush is paired with when sweeping up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the scoop that comes paired with a hand brush for sweeping.

clue.text: Fool gets told off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An idiot gets a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Legal writer possibly heard as operator with money and gold watch

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that, spoken, could pass for the first part of the name

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients
or is gold in heraldry
a timer is a watch or clock that times things

explanation.surface: A legal author might be mistaken for a surgeon with cash and a gold watch.
explanation.walkthrough: SURGEON said aloud sounds like SIR JOHN. Sir John Mortimer was a barrister and the author of the Rumpole of the Bailey stories.
explanation.definitionFit: John Mortimer was a practising barrister who wrote legal fiction, so he is a writer on legal matters.

clue.text: Oprah's transformation was astonishing

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun: the lighthouse is one of the Seven Wonders, things that astonish

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form of something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The TV host Oprah's makeover was remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the themed answers named in 19/20: each is defined by an adjective of wonder because each is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharos of Alexandria, a great lighthouse, was one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

clue.text: Hunter of game getting stick

parts.note: nim is a game of taking matches or counters from piles
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A hunter goes for game and gets a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name stands for any keen hunter.

clue.text: Miraculous execution with potential dangers

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun phrase: the hanging gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders

parts.note: hanging is a form of execution

indicators.note: potential suggests something not yet in its final shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An execution was miraculously survived despite all its dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the Seven Wonders listed in 19/20; 'potential' rearranges DANGERS into the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were among the Seven Wonders, marvels of the ancient world.

clue.text: Heralds' coming up for air over the Channel high — nothing in it

indicators.note: nothing goes in it, that is inside the French word for high

parts.note: across the Channel, in France, high is haut
rien is French for nothing, still over the Channel

explanation.surface: A Channel crossing at height has nothing on board, says the herald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the Channel' means French, and applies to both words. In heraldry a fish shown upright, head up as if rising for air, is described with this term.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic blazon describes a fish placed vertically with its head upward, as if breathing at the surface, with this term.

clue.text: Pre-Christian revivalist finds a space to rise into light

indicators.note: into signals the pieces going inside the light

parts.note: a neon is a light or lamp

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the words a space run backwards

parts.note: a gap is a space

explanation.surface: A believer in the old gods finds room to climb towards the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns A GAP into PAGA, which goes 'into' NEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A neopagan revives the pre-Christian religions, worshipping the old gods anew.

clue.text: In English, six tables per room follow "mighty Must" from Princess Ida

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: In an English restaurant six tables fill each room, following a line from Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan opera; one song lists 'the mighty Must, the inevitable Shall'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Princess Ida lyric the phrase directly follows 'the mighty Must', completing the pairing of necessity.

clue.text: Doubling stone for single people

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
I, the Roman one, is single
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A precious stone set aside for unmarried people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single people' reads as unmarried folk; the words split, giving one and a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemination is the doubling of a sound or letter, a term from linguistics.

clue.text: Grub — hot stuff's about right

indicators.note: about means going around, so the hot stuff surrounds the letter

parts.note: lava is hot stuff, molten rock; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Food that's spicy is just about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food, but it is the insect stage. 'about' puts LAVA round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the larva of an insect, the soft worm-like stage before the adult.

clue.text: Amazing mark on goldfish? I'm not sure

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun: the tomb at Halicarnassus was one of the Seven Wonders

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency
gold is AU, its chemical symbol, and the fish is a sole
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Is that marking on the goldfish astonishing? Not sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goldfish' splits into gold and fish. One of the Seven Wonders listed in 19/20: the tomb of Mausolus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus was one of the Seven Wonders, and gave its name to every grand tomb.

clue.text: Cornering movement catching no coppers at first

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the movement holds the other pieces

parts.note: a motion is a movement
taken as written
polis is a Scottish word for police, the coppers

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A tactic of cornering catches no police officers at first.
explanation.walkthrough: POLIS is Scottish slang for the police, and 'at first' gives just A, the opening letter of 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopolisation is cornering a market, taking exclusive control of a trade.

clue.text: Having acres on map missing page with street on it

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a plan is a map
Downing Street is the London street of the Prime Minister's residence

explanation.surface: Owning land on a map that's lost a page, with a street marked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing page' drops P from PLAN. In a down clue 'with street on it' puts DOWNING under LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Landowning means possessing land, so having acres is a plain description.

clue.text: Relative to return after 'er death

indicators.note: 'er is her with its H dying away, Cockney-style, so the same letter dies out of the haunting word

parts.note: ghosts return after death to haunt the living, so returning afterwards is haunting

explanation.surface: A relative comes back to haunt after her death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'after her death', but 'er death' works as the death of the dropped H: Cockney speech loses the H in her, and so loses it from the word too.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a relative, a parent's sister.

clue.text: Stuff for puffer in small station without a name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the station surrounds the pieces

parts.note: a halt is a small railway station with few facilities

explanation.surface: Something for a smoker is found at a little nameless station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside puts HALT round A N. A halt is a small British country railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhalant is a medicine breathed in, such as the stuff in an asthma puffer.

clue.text: Act unfriendly in the sergeant's mess

definitions.note: an imperative verb phrase: to alienate is to make someone stop being friendly

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone behaves coldly in the sergeants' mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the soldiers' dining room, but it signals the rearrangement of SERGEANT; the 's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, causing someone to become unfriendly or distant.

clue.text: Phenomenal firm, one sadly missed by the States

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun: the bronze statue at Rhodes was one of the Seven Wonders

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a loss is someone mourned, sadly missed
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A phenomenal company, sorely missed in America.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the Seven Wonders listed in 19/20: the Colossus of Rhodes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colossus of Rhodes, a vast bronze statue, was one of the Seven Wonders of antiquity.

clue.text: Return of prizes measure as check to swinging

indicators.note: return means going back, so the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: pots are prizes, trophies
a rood is an old measure of land

explanation.surface: Getting the prizes back is a measure that checks swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is an old British land measure of a quarter acre; 'Return of' reverses both pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstop is a wedge or block stopping a door from swinging.

clue.text: Voice trial — took part

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the words is used, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A voice test was undergone.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singing voice, the lowest female or highest male range.

clue.text: Capital game preferred by Sir Roger de Coverley to 5 25, 10, 3, 16 and 22

definitions.text: preferred by Sir Roger de Coverley to 5 25, 10, 3, 16 and 22

parts.note: London is the British capital
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: The capital's game was preferred by an old squire to ancient marvels.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Roger de Coverley, the squire in Addison's Spectator essays, rated London's bridge above the Seven Wonders, which are the cross-referenced answers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Spectator, Sir Roger judged the Thames crossing a finer marvel than the Seven Wonders of the World.

clue.text: See 19
Such as Cotman and Corot rule out being in the middle

indicators.note: being in signals the scrambled letters going inside the middle

parts.note: the waist is the middle of the body

indicators.note: out suggests being out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two painters, Cotman and Corot, refuse to be placed centrally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corot' looks like part of the definition but is fodder: 'out' rearranges COROT RULE into TERCOLOUR, 'being in' WAIST.
explanation.definitionFit: John Sell Cotman was an English painter famous for his watercolours.

clue.text: Backwater with stupendous statue

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Suez is the canal, a stretch of water

explanation.surface: A remote backwater has an enormous statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backwater' splits into Back and water. One of the Seven Wonders listed in 19/20: Pheidias' statue at Olympia.
explanation.definitionFit: The great statue of the chief god at Olympia was one of the Seven Wonders.

clue.text: Setter's thought about six counties being protected

parts.note: the setter's 'I am' contracts to I'm

indicators.note: about means around, so the thought surrounds the counties

parts.note: mused means thought
Northern Ireland, NI, is made up of six counties

explanation.surface: The setter has been thinking about Northern Ireland while kept safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The six counties are the ones forming Northern Ireland, a common crossword route to NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being immunised means being protected against a disease by vaccination.

clue.text: Customary title for primate is a cover

parts.note: Dr is a common title, for a doctor
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An archbishop's usual form of address turns out to be a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' and 'title' suggest an archbishop's honorific, but the primate is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a cloth hung as a cover or curtain.

clue.text: See 5
Eyed sewers near fresh water?

definitions.meaning: sewing tools with an eye for the thread
the chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight lie near Freshwater, a village on the island

explanation.surface: Sewing tools with eyes are kept beside clean water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' reads as drains but means things that sew. Freshwater is a village on the Isle of Wight, close to the chalk stacks of the same name as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are eyed tools for sewing, and the Needles are rocks off the Isle of Wight.
